# `silk/yaml/output`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Write YAML text: a whole `YamlDocument`, or values one at a time with `YamlEmitter`.

## When to use
Use [`YamlOutput.write`](#YamlOutput.impl.write) to write a parsed `silk.yaml.document.YamlDocument` back as text. Use
[`YamlEmitter`](#YamlEmitter) to write YAML from a program's own data, value by value. Use
`silk.schema.yaml.SchemaYaml.encode` to write a typed value.

## Details
The output is block style: each mapping entry and each sequence item is on its own line, and
nested collections are indented by two spaces. An empty mapping is written as `{}` and an empty
sequence as `[]`. A string is written plain (without quotes) when a YAML 1.2 reader reads the
plain text back as the same string, and a YAML 1.1 reader does too: `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`,
`y`, `n`, dates such as `2001-12-14`, and numbers such as `12:30` and `1_000` are quoted. A string with line breaks is written as a literal block scalar (`|`).
All other strings are double-quoted, with escapes for control characters and line separators.
Floats are written with the shortest text that reads back to the same value, and a whole float
keeps a `.0` so it stays a float.

The text goes to the ambient `Writer` in pieces of up to 4 KiB.

## Examples
### Write a mapping
```silk
import silk.collections.slice { Slice }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }
import silk.yaml.document { YamlError }
import silk.yaml.output { YamlEmitter }

struct Capture {
  bytes: [u8; 128],
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for Capture {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, val: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer {
    Slice.copyInto<u8>(&mut self.bytes, self.length, val)
    self.length = self.length + val.length
    return ()
  }
  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer { return () }
}

effect fn emit() -> () ! YamlError | WriterError ? &mut Writer {
  let mut emitter = YamlEmitter.make()
  run emitter.beginMapping()
  run emitter.key("name")
  run emitter.text("Ada")
  run emitter.key("ports")
  run emitter.beginSequence()
  run emitter.element()
  run emitter.signed(80)
  run emitter.element()
  run emitter.signed(443)
  run emitter.endSequence()
  run emitter.endMapping()
  return run emitter.finish()
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! YamlError | WriterError {
  let mut capture = Capture {bytes: [0; 128], length: 0}
  run emit() |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut capture)
  if Slice.view<u8>(&capture.bytes, 0, capture.length) != b"name: Ada\nports:\n  - 80\n  - 443\n" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="YamlOutput.impl.write"></a>

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write(document: &YamlDocument) -> () ! YamlError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes every document of `document` as YAML text to the ambient `Writer`, and a `---` line
before each document after the first. A stream with no documents writes nothing.

#### Details

The text is block style, with two spaces of indentation. Strings are written plain when that
reads back as the same string, as a literal block scalar (`|`) when they hold line breaks, and
double-quoted otherwise. Comments, anchors, tags, and the source style of each value are not
kept: a value that an alias copied is written in full. The text goes to the `Writer` in pieces
of up to 4 KiB. It does not flush the `Writer`.

#### Errors

- `YamlError` with reason `YamlReason.DepthExceeded` if the collections nest more than
  `MAX_DEPTH` (128) levels deep, which aliases can cause. Its `offset` is 0.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails. Bytes that it accepted before the failure stay written.

#### Examples

```silk
import silk.collections.slice { Slice }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.yaml.document { YamlDocument, YamlError }
import silk.yaml.output { YamlOutput }

struct Capture {
  bytes: [u8; 128],
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for Capture {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, val: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer {
    Slice.copyInto<u8>(&mut self.bytes, self.length, val)
    self.length = self.length + val.length
    return ()
  }
  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer { return () }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! YamlError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let document = run YamlDocument.parse(b"{name: Ada, tags: [a, 'b c']}") |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let mut capture = Capture {bytes: [0; 128], length: 0}
  run YamlOutput.write(&document) |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut capture)
  if Slice.view<u8>(&capture.bytes, 0, capture.length) != b"name: Ada\ntags:\n  - a\n  - b c\n" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="YamlEmitter"></a>

## `YamlEmitter`

```silk
pub struct YamlEmitter
```

Writes YAML text to the ambient `Writer`, one value at a time, in block style.

### When to use

Write YAML from a program's own data without building a `YamlDocument` first. Use
[`YamlOutput.write`](#YamlOutput.impl.write) for a document you have.

### Details

Start a mapping with `beginMapping`, then call `key` before each value and `endMapping` at the
end. Start a sequence with `beginSequence`, then call `element` before each value and
`endSequence` at the end. A value is a scalar (`null`, `boolean`, `signed`, `unsigned`, `float`,
`text`) or a nested collection. One document is one value; call `nextDocument` to start another,
and `finish` at the end. Nested collections are indented by two spaces, an empty mapping is `{}`,
and an empty sequence is `[]`. A string is written plain when a reader reads it back as the same
string, as a literal block scalar (`|`) when it holds line breaks, and double-quoted otherwise.
The text is kept in a 4 KiB buffer that goes to the `Writer` when it is full and at `finish`.

### Gotchas

- Call `finish` after the last value, or the end of the text stays in the buffer.
- Calls out of order trap: a value with no `key` or `element` before it in a collection, a `key`
  outside a mapping, an `element` outside a sequence, a `key` or `element` before the last one has
  its value, a second value in one document, or an end call that does not match the open
  collection.

### Examples

```silk
import silk.collections.slice { Slice }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }
import silk.yaml.document { YamlError }
import silk.yaml.output { YamlEmitter }

struct Capture {
  bytes: [u8; 128],
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for Capture {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, val: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer {
    Slice.copyInto<u8>(&mut self.bytes, self.length, val)
    self.length = self.length + val.length
    return ()
  }
  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer { return () }
}

effect fn emit() -> () ! YamlError | WriterError ? &mut Writer {
  let mut emitter = YamlEmitter.make()
  run emitter.beginSequence()
  run emitter.element()
  run emitter.beginMapping()
  run emitter.key("on")
  run emitter.boolean(true)
  run emitter.key("note")
  run emitter.text("line one\nline two\n")
  run emitter.endMapping()
  run emitter.endSequence()
  return run emitter.finish()
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! YamlError | WriterError {
  let mut capture = Capture {bytes: [0; 128], length: 0}
  run emit() |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut capture)
  if Slice.view<u8>(&capture.bytes, 0, capture.length) != b"- \"on\": true\n  note: |\n    line one\n    line two\n" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="YamlEmitter.impl.float"></a>

### Method `float`

```silk
pub effect fn float(self: &mut Self, value: f64) -> () ! YamlError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes the float with the shortest text that reads back to the same value.

#### Details

A whole number keeps a fraction, as `2.0`, so it reads back as a float. An exponent comes after
a fraction and has a sign, as in `1.0e+30`, so YAML 1.1 readers read it too. A NaN is written
as `.nan`, and the infinities as `.inf` and `-.inf`.

#### Errors

- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails while the buffer is written out.

<a id="YamlEmitter.impl.text"></a>

### Method `text`

```silk
pub effect fn text(self: &mut Self, value: string) -> () ! YamlError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes the string: plain when a reader reads it back as the same string, as a literal block
scalar (`|`) when it holds line breaks, and double-quoted otherwise.

#### Details

Text that a reader would take for another kind of value, such as `true`, `12`, or `null`, is
quoted, as is text that a YAML 1.1 reader takes for another value: `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`,
`y`, `n`, dates such as `2001-12-14`, and numbers such as `12:30` and `1_000`. Double-quoted text
escapes `"`, `\`, control characters, and the Unicode line separators.

#### Errors

- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails while the buffer is written out.


<a id="YamlEmitter.impl.key"></a>

### Method `key`

```silk
pub effect fn key(self: &mut Self, name: string) -> () ! YamlError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes the key of the next entry of the open mapping, and `:`.

#### Details

The key is plain or double-quoted by the rules of `text`; a key with line breaks is
double-quoted. A key longer than 1000 bytes is written as an explicit key (`? key`), because
YAML limits other keys to 1024 characters. The emitter does not check that keys are unique.

#### Errors

- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails while the buffer is written out.

#### Gotchas

Traps if the innermost open collection is not a mapping, or the last key has no value.

#### Errors

#### Gotchas

Traps if the innermost open collection is not a mapping, or its last key has no value.

<a id="YamlEmitter.impl.nextDocument"></a>

### Method `nextDocument`

```silk
pub effect fn nextDocument(self: &mut Self) -> () ! YamlError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Ends the current document with a `---` line, so that the next value starts a new document.

#### Details

A document with no value is written as `null`.

#### Errors

- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails while the buffer is written out.

#### Gotchas

Traps if a collection is still open.

<a id="YamlEmitter.impl.finish"></a>

### Method `finish`

```silk
pub effect fn finish(self: &mut Self) -> () ! YamlError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes the rest of the buffer to the `Writer`. It does not flush the `Writer`.

#### Details

A document with no value is written as `null`. The emitter can write more values after it
only after `nextDocument`.

#### Errors

- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails. Bytes that it accepted before the failure stay written.

#### Gotchas

Traps if a collection is still open.
